newsitem.title: ITALY: ATHLETICS-BOULMERKA OUT OF MEDITERRANEAN GAMES.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BOULMERKA OUT OF MEDITERRANEAN GAMES.

text.p: Former Olympic gold medalist Hassiba Boulmerka pulled out of the Mediterranean Games on Tuesday after injuring her leg in training, the head of the Algerian delegation said.
"She has a problem with her leg. She is in a training camp in Germany and her doctor informed us. It's a recurring problem," Amar Brahmia said.

Boulmerka's absence from the 1,500 metres denied the four-yearly games its biggest name, with many of the top athletes from the 21 participating Mediterranean nations staying away to prepare for August's world championships in Athens.
"The most important thing for Hassiba is to prepare for the world championships," Brahnia said.

Boulmerka, who won gold at the Barcelona Olympics in 1992 but pulled out of the 1,500 metre finals at Atlanta last year after a bad fall, had been billed by organisers as the top attraction at the 13th Mediterranean Games.

The Algerian shot to fame after winning the first world title by an African woman in the 1991 Tokyo championships. Moslem fundamentalists, outraged to see Boulmerka running in bare legs, sent her death threats after the victory.

Dionisio Ciccarese, communications director of the Mediterranean Games, said the poor turn-out of leading athletes was because regional events were being hit by the bigger cash-rich international meetings.
"With the international competitions, regional games such as the Mediterranean games and the Pan-American games are penalised. It's a handicap," Ciccarese said.
He added that the tight schedule running up to the world championships in two months meant long-distance runners could not be expected to also compete at Bari.

Brahmia said Algeria, home to some of the world's top middle distance runners, considered the Mediterranean Games a training ground for its young athletes rather than a serious international competition.

For this reason Algeria, which has won two golds so far in the marathon and swimming with the men's 100 metres freestyle, had not entered world 1,500 metre record holder and men's Olympic champion Noureddine Morceli.
"It's not the level of Noureddine Morceli," Brahnia said. "He would kill all the other athletes".
Morceli won the 1,500 metres gold at the last Mediterranean Games in France four years ago.
After the third day of competition in 27 disciplines, Italy headed the medal table with 20 golds. Turkey was in second place with 14 golds and France third with 12.

Bari's San Nicola stadium, built for the 1990 soccer World Cup finals, was almost completely empty on Monday for the opening track events, with athletes and organisational staff outnumbering spectators.
The highlight was a convincing 5,000 metres win by Italian Roberta Brunet, a bronze medalist at the Atlanta Olympics last year, who clocked 15 minutes 00.69 seconds.

Greece's Angelos Pavlakakis won the men's 100 metres in 10.13 seconds, not an exceptional time but given resonance by the fact that it broke one of Italian Pietro Mennea's last remaining international records.
Mennea's record of 10.15 was set in Split in 1979.
British-born Italian Fiona May decided to stay away from the women's long jump competition and the men's 5,000 metres was without Moroccan Olympic silver medallist Khalid Boulami.
Olympic 200 metres champion Marie-Jose Perec of France and heptathlete Ghada Shousa, who won Syria's first gold medal in its Olympic history at Atlanta, were also absent.
